Image created by ChatGPTThe next data workflow is not “AI writes SQL.” It is “humans define intent, context, constraints, and evidence — then agents execute inside those boundaries.”
Imagine opening a pull request at 8:30 on a Monday morning. During the night, an agent inspected the data sources it was allowed to use, traced the relevant dbt lineage, proposed a model at the right grain, generated the SQL, added tests and documentation, ran the build, found a reconciliation error, repaired the transformation, reran the checks, and attached an evidence report.
Your first task is not to write the model again.
Your task is to review the assumptions, challenge the business interpretation, inspect the evidence, and decide whether the change is safe to merge. That is not the end of analytics engineering. It is a change in its unit of work.
The traditional unit of work was often a file: a SQL model, a YAML definition, a test, a dashboard calculation, or a pipeline task. In an agentic workflow, the unit of work becomes a governed change: a business intent executed by software inside a defined context, with explicit permissions, quality gates, and human accountability.
This is why I believe the analytics engineer is becoming an agent manager.
